items.summary: The finding was confirmed in the current code: ReadLaunchAdmissionForBudget kept a stand-in count of one running client for a row held for a Roblox update for as long as process samples were untrusted, so after a long monitoring failure the row still said "This request starts on its own once no Roblox client is running" even when no client ran. The stand-in now lasts only while the newest trusted (fresh, complete) process inventory is at most ClientUpdateHold.UntrustedSampleGrace old (6 s, twice LaunchReservationProjection.MaximumEvidenceAge, measured from that inventory's observation time). The Shell notes the newest trusted inventory lock-free in both the 1 Hz sampler and admission (a monotonic CAS on a long), so alternating fresh/untrusted samples on a busy PC still neither re-save nor re-word the row (the N-B8-4 rule is kept), while a failure that outlasts the grace returns the row to the ordinary "fresh complete process evidence is required" wait (row text "Waiting for fresh measurements and sufficient resource headroom"); the next fresh sample with a client running holds it again. Starts stay refused on every untrusted sample, as before. items.summary: Zenith can now clean up old Roblox Player logs on demand, in two explicit steps on the Diagnostics page (expander "Roblox client logs"): "Check old logs" counts the *_Player_*.log files older than the days the user chooses (1 to 365, default 7) directly inside the documented Roblox log roots below LocalApplicationData and shows their total size; "Delete these logs…" is enabled only after a check that found something, the view asks a question naming that same count and size (permanent, not Recycle Bin), and the delete removes exactly the checked files, each re-checked just before it goes. A log is always kept when it is newer than the cutoff, when the log correlator is watching it (new WindowsSessionLogCorrelator.WatchedLogPaths: discovered candidates and bound logs; a cutoff under one day is refused because the correlator discovers logs written within a day), or when another process holds it open (the check opens each file sharing only deletion, which Windows refuses while a client holds it; the delete is the same open with delete-on-close, so a running client's log cannot be taken). Studio logs are never touched, nothing is read from the logs, no path enters diagnostics, Roblox's settings are untouched, nothing runs on its own (no setting is saved), Panic/Lock/Cancel/exit stop a check or delete and drop the checked list, and the sample profile keeps the tool off. items.summary: Zenith can now check for Roblox updates on its own and install the official update, both as the owner described. Settings > Roblox installation gains "Check for Roblox updates automatically" (saved setting CheckRobloxUpdates, default off): 3 seconds after the manager is ready and every 30 minutes after each check, Zenith makes the same anonymous read of Roblox's public version service that Refresh installation makes (a full refresh when no row is selected; release-only, filling the rows in place, when a row is selected so a trial installation is kept) and announces a pending update once per release. "Download Roblox update" fetches Roblox's own installer for that release from setup.rbxcdn.com (address built only from a valid upload name; one anonymous GET with no redirects, cookie, User-Agent, Referer or Origin; 64 MB and 5-minute bounds) into a fresh %TEMP% folder and verifies it with the existing WindowsClientExecutableTrust path (cached-evidence Authenticode, Roblox Corporation publisher, double SHA-256, re-open comparison), then holds the verified file open sharing read only so it cannot be rewritten, renamed or deleted before it runs; anything not verified is deleted. "Install Roblox update" asks first (release, verified publisher, how many Roblox clients are running and that the installer closes every one), then runs the held file with no arguments and waits up to 10 minutes; Zenith never ends the installer, and refreshes the installation list after a normal exit. Panic and Lock cancel the work and discard a held installer; Lock idles the check until Unlock; exit joins the work. This one feature covers R-shell-19 as well. The release summary's "Zenith never downloads or installs updates" wording was reversed per the owner's decision.

items.summary: The finding was confirmed against the current code: ObserveClientSoundArrivals carried an unreadable PID forward only when a key with that PID was already in _soundSeenClients, so a client Windows could not read in the first accepted scan (for example Zenith starting with "Mute clients when they appear" already saved on), or in any scan while the preference was off or paused, was never recorded and was muted as a new arrival when a later scan first read it. The shell now keeps a second small set, _soundUnreadClients: the PIDs the last accepted scan could not read that were first listed while nothing was watched. A readable row whose PID is in that set is treated as already known, not an arrival; the set is re-intersected with each scan's unreadable PIDs (and extended by them only while not watching), so it is bounded by one scan (at most 128) and a PID that is gone can be reused by a genuinely new client. A client first listed unreadable while watching is still muted once a scan reads it. The design doc paragraph on arrival muting records the rule; the Guide sentence already said clients already running are left alone, so it was not changed.

A side effect for users: a wall-clock change can no longer shorten or extend the window. No user-facing wording, settings or defaults changed.

items.summary: Zenith gains a hard per-client CPU cap, the RoALT capability the owner approved. A new Sessions action, Cap CPU (default off), puts each checked client in a Windows job this run creates and holds the only handle to (JOB_OBJECT_CPU_RATE_CONTROL_ENABLE | HARD_CAP, never KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE) and limits that client's threads together to a chosen share of all CPU time (10/25/50/75%, per click, never saved); Windows lowers its frame rate as a side effect. It touches nothing in the client's files or settings. The cap joins the same bounded ownership as the priority/efficiency/core controls, so Restore original, Exit, observed-conflict refusal, Stop/Lock/Panic and the 128-entry cap all apply; because Windows keeps a process in its job for life, Restore clears the job's rate control and leaves the client in the now-inert job. RoALT's conceded weakness (an unnamed job's cap cannot be lifted after a kill) is addressed: each capped client's exact instance is recorded in client-cpu-caps.json before the job is used, and the next start names the clients its record says still carry a cap a crashed run could not clear (no later run can reach that job) and tells the user to close and reopen them, while dropping records of exited clients. A client already in a Windows job this run did not create is reported AlreadyInJob and left alone.

items.summary: Close on a Sessions row now runs an escalating close: after the existing confirmation, Zenith posts WM_CLOSE to the identity-checked client window, posts again after 400 ms so Roblox's own leave prompt is answered, and waits 6 s on the exact process's own exit (a registered wait on a SYNCHRONIZE duplicate of the process handle, never a poll); it never ends the process itself. A client still open after that wait gets a Force close button on its row only; the window asks a second confirmation that names the client (PID and start time, No is the default), then TerminateProcess runs on a fresh handle whose creation time was checked against the observed start and whose executable is a Roblox client, and the accepted termination is recorded in Recent clients as a forced end (new optional Forced field in the history evidence column; the fourteen-field payload that pre-evidence builds read is unchanged) that outranks every other end cause. Nothing is automatic and there is no batch: Panic, Lock and exit cancel every waiting close and withdraw every offer; the normal close stays available under lock, the force-close offer does not. Monitors without the control (sample mode, test fakes) keep the single request, so no existing fake or test changed.

items.summary: Zenith Sessions now has an opt-in upload limit for all Roblox clients together, as the owner approved: Sessions > Upload limit takes a whole rate (100 to 10,000,000 kbit/s) and offers Apply upload limit, Remove and Cancel. Apply and Remove each run Windows PowerShell 5.1 as administrator through the UAC prompt the user answers (ShellExecute runas, the fixed script passed as an encoded command with only the checked integer in it, no -ExecutionPolicy Bypass); the script creates one New-NetQosPolicy per observed client executable (RobloxPlayerBeta.exe, RobloxPlayer.exe, Roblox.exe) in the ActiveStore only, reads each back and reports through its exit code (0 confirmed, 3 readback mismatch, else refused); Remove deletes them and confirms by listing the store with Stop, so a denied read can never pass as success. Because reading the ActiveStore needs administrator rights (verified: unelevated Get-NetQosPolicy is denied), "the current policy" is Zenith's own record for this Windows session (upload-limit.json: action, rate, time, confirmed, boot time; dropped after a Windows restart), and the section says in words when that record is uncertain (a refused, unconfirmed, timed-out or stopped run) or unreadable. Default off: nothing is ever applied without the click and the prompt; the policy is not removed on exit and ends when Windows restarts; one operation at a time; Cancel, Panic, Lock and exit stop the wait (a run already approved finishes on its own and the status says so). No client file, setting or memory is touched and no Roblox request is made; failures are typed statuses recorded against a new ManagerSubsystem.UploadLimit.

items.summary: Zenith Sessions can now post Discord webhook alerts (also covers R-shell-22). Settings → Appearance gains "Send Discord alerts" (schema-1 DiscordAlerts, default off, applied after Save settings), a masked webhook field with Save/Clear webhook, Send test alert and Resume alerts. When on, a fixed-template message goes to the one saved webhook when a client crashes (Windows fault record, or weaker a crash dump), stops responding, or is disconnected (not the player's own leave; "account launched elsewhere" is named), and when a launch batch has every request settled; messages carry only account labels, places and counts, built from Zenith's own presence history and launch queue. The URL is accepted only as https on discord.com/discordapp.com (plus ptb/canary) with the /api/webhooks/<id>/<token> shape, is held pinned and zeroed, stored DPAPI-protected in discord-webhook.dat, read per send, and shown as host plus the token's last four; it never enters settings, logs, exports or diagnostics. Sends are coalesced (alerts within 2 s share one message of up to 10 lines), bounded (50 queued, oldest dropped and counted) and paced (one message per 2 s); a 429 waits once for Discord's bounded Retry-After; any other failure is recorded by type against the new Discord alerts subsystem and shown once until a send succeeds, never retried; a webhook Discord refuses (401/403/404) stops alerts until a new URL is saved. Panic stops the outbox (dropping queued alerts, cancelling the send in flight) until Resume alerts or the choice is saved on after being off; Lock leaves it running because monitoring continues behind the lock; Exit cancels and disposes the transport and store; sample mode never sends. The client sends Zenith's own Zenith-Sessions/<version> User-Agent, no Referer/Origin, no redirects, no cookies, and never reads the response body.

items.summary: Zenith now has a second, selectable native launch mode, "Direct ticket", next to the official-page capture, which stays the default (Settings → Roblox installation → Native launch mode; optional schema-1 NativeLaunchMode = official-page | direct-ticket, old files load unchanged, an unknown value is refused). In that mode a trial asks Roblox for the client assertion and an authentication ticket with the account's saved sign-in (RobloxLaunchTicketClient: GET auth.roblox.com/v1/client-assertion/ then POST auth.roblox.com/v1/authentication-ticket/, same discipline as the share-link resolver: exact endpoints, no redirects, no cookie jar, per-identity CSRF token kept in memory with one retry, 64 KiB cap, 20 s deadline, 401 → sign-in required, human check → challenge, 403 → refused, 429 → rate limited; User-Agent "ZenithSessions/0.50", never a Referer or Origin; RBXAuthenticationNegotiation only on the ticket POST), builds the roblox-player request itself for the frozen destination (play mode, PlaceLauncher RequestGame/RequestGameJob, launchtime now, fresh browser tracker kept for log linking, fresh join attempt, empty channel) and accepts it through the same grammar the page capture validates (NativeRobloxHandoff.AcceptBuilt), so nothing is rewritten after validation and no page opens or click is needed. The ticket is a one-use pinned ProtectedLaunchTicket, zeroed after use, never logged, persisted, exported or shown. It sits behind the existing IRobloxNativeHandoffCapture seam (SelectableNativeHandoffCapture reads the saved mode once per preparation), so the preparer's same-player verification and final grant, publisher trust, account binding, admission, pacing, Panic/Lock (which also forget the kept CSRF tokens) and one start at a time are unchanged; Launch evidence, the trial review and status, settings search and the Guide name the mode and the typed ticket refusals. Also covers R-launch-13 (no window per account). Default off: official page remains the saved default until the live trial verifies the direct mode.

items.summary: Zenith can now launch through an installed bootstrapper (Bloxstrap, Fishstrap, Froststrap or Voidstrap; Voidstrap discovery was added) when the user selects that bootstrapper's own row under Settings → Roblox installation.
